clue.text: Incentive to reveal vehicular rust

parts.note: vehicular points to a car, the everyday vehicle
rust is rot or decay eating into metal

explanation.surface: Someone finds a corroded car and calls the discovery a reward.
explanation.definitionFit: The carrot dangled before a donkey is the classic image of a reward offered to motivate.

clue.text: Collected and wrote notes

explanation.definitionFit: A calm person is cool and unflustered; a composer creates music by writing it.

clue.text: Dawn of Japanese standardisation

definitions.meaning: dawn is daybreak, when the sun comes up
the Japanese standard, or flag, shows the emblem of daybreak

explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is when the sun comes over the horizon; Japan's flag bears that sun.

clue.text: Means of propulsion on a Roman ship, originally

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: How a Roman galley was driven forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Oars push a rowing boat through the water by rowing.

clue.text: Joy, Sue, Pearl, Dotty

indicators.note: dotty means crazy or scatty, so the two names are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of three women's names, one of them eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy and delight are close synonyms for the feeling of enjoyment.

clue.text: Window in the French garret

indicators.note: in places the garret inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
a garret is an attic room

explanation.surface: A window in the French artist's attic room.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice window has small diamond panes set in a criss-cross frame.

clue.text: Publicity given to official run

indicators.note: given to joins the official after the publicity

parts.note: an ad is an advert, publicity
a minister is a government official

explanation.surface: A government officer is handed a publicity campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer a business or department is to manage or run it.

clue.text: Relative takes the pledge

definitions.meaning: a parent's brother is a family relative
old slang for the pawnbroker, who takes goods as pledges

explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a relative; uncle was slang for a pawnbroker holding pledges.

clue.text: England's first slip gets run out

indicators.note: first takes the initial letter of England's

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: England's first slip fielder ends up run out in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: a slip is a fielder near the batsman and run out is a dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes or expires, as a deadline runs out.

clue.text: Take revenge in the denouement

definitions.meaning: to pay someone off can mean to settle a score with them
the denouement is the final twist that resolves a story

explanation.definitionFit: A payoff is a story's climax or outcome; to pay off a score is to get even.

clue.text: Criminal worker found after awful crimes

indicators.note: found after says the worker piece follows the scrambled letters
awful suggests the word crimes is mangled into a new order

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A labourer is caught after committing dreadful offences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as an adjective for the worker, but it is the noun definition; 'awful' scrambles the clue's crimes (MISCRE) and 'found after' sets the insect behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer or villain, the noun sense of criminal.

clue.text: Holy city came about within a century

indicators.note: within places the century letter inside the rearranged letters
about signals the letters of came being turned around into a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: Someone arrived at a sacred city around a hundred years ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges CAME as MECA, and 'within' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mecca in Saudi Arabia is the holiest city of Islam, the goal of pilgrimage.

clue.text: The sound of a pig at home in agreeable surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the agreeable word wraps round the at-home word

parts.note: OK means all right, acceptable
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A pig makes a noise while comfortable in pleasant quarters at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A grunt is the noise associated with swine in cartoons and nursery talk.

clue.text: Still waiting for proposals?

definitions.meaning: still means not moving at all
a meeting with no proposals put to it is without a motion, read as a playful compound

explanation.definitionFit: Being still means being without movement, stationary and unmoving.

clue.text: Swimmer's given beer? Rubbish!

parts.note: the cod is a swimmer, a fish; the possessive gives the s
wallop is British slang for beer

explanation.surface: A fish is offered a pint, and someone shouts nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: WALLOP is old British slang for beer; codswallop is British for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is British slang for nonsense or drivel.

clue.text: Change of fee as required to relieve tension

indicators.note: Change tells us to rearrange the letters that follow

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Altering a charge when needed to calm a tense negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required to' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken or lessen pressure is to reduce strain, as on a rope or a situation.

clue.text: Guarantee Rex is about to succeed? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: is about would put the king's letter round the verb, a container
Quite the opposite reverses which piece goes inside which

parts.note: to ensue is to follow on, succeed
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the king is on the point of triumphing, then contradicts it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, R would hold ENSUE; 'Quite the opposite' flips it so ENSUE holds R.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain of something is to guarantee it will happen.

clue.text: Taking ill, the new nurse left

indicators.note: new says the letters are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Falling sick, the newly hired nurse departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking ill' reads as falling sick, but means taking something badly, offended.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a remark ill is to be offended by it, feeling bitter.

clue.text: Object about wrongdoers being supported

annotationWithheld.why: Object about wrongdoers being supported (8): the parse END around an anagram of DOERS splits the single word 'wrongdoers' into indicator 'wrong' and fodder 'doers', which the grammar cannot express.

clue.text: Wrongly spelt noun one's found in agreement

indicators.note: found in places the one's piece inside the jumbled letters
spelt wrongly says the letters of noun are jumbled

parts.note: one's is I'S, the numeral I with the s

explanation.surface: A grammatical slip: a noun has been misspelt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in agreement' tempts as the definition phrase, but 'in' belongs to 'found in', which inserts; 'Wrongly spelt' jumbles the noun into UNON.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing in unison means together as one, hence harmony or accord.

clue.text: Not one of two or three in disorder

indicators.note: in disorder says the words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Not one of two, or of three, in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neither means not either of a pair.

clue.text: After start of trial, argue cause of crime

indicators.note: After says the next piece comes behind the opening letter
start of picks the opening letter of trial

parts.note: to reason is to argue a case or cause logically

explanation.surface: Once a trial opens, a lawyer argues what drove the offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the offence of betraying one's country, a grave crime.

clue.text: Temporary shelter in which there's an occupant

indicators.note: in which says the article sits inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is living in a makeshift shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is a person who occupies rented property.

clue.text: Chemical result of smoking cannabis?

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
ash is what's left after smoking

explanation.surface: What chemical is left after a joint is smoked?
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is potassium carbonate, a chemical once made from wood ash.

clue.text: Unconscious and long-suffering with travelling case

parts.note: someone knocked out is out
long-suffering means enduring patiently

explanation.surface: A stoic, out-cold traveller with a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is a medical case, not luggage: a patient who travels to hospital and goes home the same day.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital case who visits for treatment without staying overnight comes and goes.

clue.text: Monster fish?

definitions.meaning: a giant or ogre from Scandinavian folklore
to fish by trailing a baited line

explanation.definitionFit: A troll is a Norse ogre; trolling is fishing with a line drawn behind a boat.

clue.text: Free from any sound of noise pollution

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Being released from any noise pollution at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'sound of'; 'noise pollution' only pads the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie or unfasten a knot or a prisoner is to set loose.

clue.text: Keen to help a number inside

indicators.note: inside puts the number within the help word

parts.note: aid means help
C is the Roman numeral 100, a number

explanation.surface: Eager to help a figure within.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid wit is sharp and biting, as a keen blade is sharp.

clue.text: Everybody is about to read Coral Island

indicators.note: is about says everybody wraps round the small word

parts.note: everybody means all
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everyone is about to read the novel Coral Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coral Island' looks like a book title (Ballantyne's The Coral Island) but defines a reef ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped reef island built of coral.

clue.text: Worker strikes result in restriction of movement

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
cuffs are blows, light strikes

explanation.surface: Industrial action by workers leads to curbs on their freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuffs locked on the wrists stop a prisoner's arms moving freely.

clue.text: Her pilot circles round the landing platform

indicators.note: circling round suggests the letters spin into a new order

explanation.surface: A female pilot circles before touching down on the pad.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliport is a place where helicopters take off and land.

clue.text: Confused tot given guidance

parts.note: to tot up is to add
someone given guidance is led

explanation.surface: A muddled toddler is shown the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled means muddled, unable to think clearly.
